paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates vocabulary size as a function of the number of iterations for three languages: Spanish, Korean, and Japanese. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Iterations," has a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 500, and has tick labels at intervals of 100 units. The y-axis is labeled "Vocabulary Size," uses a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 5000, and has tick labels at intervals of 500 units. The plot contains three lines: a solid blue line representing Spanish, a solid orange line representing Korean, and a solid green line representing Japanese. Each line begins at the origin with a vocabulary size of 0 at 0 iterations. The blue line reaches approximately 3000 vocabulary size at 500 iterations, showing a steady increase throughout. The orange line ends near a vocabulary size of 2900 at 500 iterations, also with a consistent upward trend. Similarly, the green line concludes around a vocabulary size of 3100 at 500 iterations, maintaining a steady increase from start to finish. There is also a gray line that appears to serve as a reference, illustrating a direct proportionality between iterations and vocabulary size, intersecting points such as (0,0) and (500,5000). A legend is available on top left of the plot to identify different lines with their labels.
